rules.description: Use commas before and after subordinate clauses introduced by conjunctions such as 'że', 'aby', 'gdy', 'kiedy', 'choć', 'podczas gdy'.
Do not use a comma before 'i', 'oraz', 'a', 'ani' connecting equal clauses, unless they are repeated or introduce contrast.
Separate introductory phrases or interjections with commas.
Use commas around participial phrases (imiesłowy przysłówkowe).
Use commas to enclose non-restrictive appositions.
rules.example_correct: Jan Kowalski, mój sąsiad, wyjechał wczoraj.
rules.example_incorrect: Jan Kowalski mój sąsiad wyjechał wczoraj.

rules.description: Separate elements in a list or series with commas.
rules.example_correct: Kupił jabłka, gruszki, śliwki i banany.
rules.example_incorrect: Kupił jabłka gruszki śliwki i banany.

rules.description: End declarative sentences with a period.
Use a period in abbreviations unless the last letter is also the last letter of the word.
Use semicolons to separate items in a list when the items themselves contain commas.
rules.example_correct: Na spotkaniu byli: Jan Kowalski, prezes firmy; Anna Nowak, dyrektor; oraz Piotr Lis, sekretarz.
rules.example_incorrect: Na spotkaniu byli: Jan Kowalski, prezes firmy, Anna Nowak, dyrektor, oraz Piotr Lis, sekretarz.

rules.description: Use a colon to introduce explanations, quotations, or lists.
Use em dash (myślnik) with spaces to mark interruptions or parenthetical remarks.
rules.example_correct: To był on — mój dawny przyjaciel.

rules.description: Use dash at the start of spoken lines in dialogues instead of quotation marks.
Use hyphen (łącznik) without spaces in compound adjectives like 'czarno-biały'.
Use hyphen to connect numbers and unit symbols in complex forms, e.g. 'ISO-8859-2'.
Use Polish quotation marks: „ … ” for outer quotes, and ‘ … ’ for nested quotes.
Use ellipsis to indicate omission or unfinished thought. No space before, one space after.
No space before comma, period, semicolon, or colon; one space after.
Use spaces around em dash in Polish text; none around hyphen.
Use non-breaking space between number and unit (e.g. '5 kg').
